hints: Is there an order in which you can visit a search tree's nodes that produces its values sorted?
Left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree - the in-order walk. A search tree walked that way is sorted.
So the answer is the `k`-th node the walk visits, and the walk can stop as soon as it has counted `k`.
Stopping early is why the iterative walk is worth writing: it costs O(depth + k) rather than O(n), and for small `k` on a large tree that is most of the work saved.
